exEn: My job is interesting.

ex: Lavoro in un ufficio a Milano.
exEn: I work in an office in Milan.
What is your profession?
Anna is a colleague of mine.
note: Same form for both genders: il collega / la collega. Plural: i colleghi, le colleghe.

ex: Il mio capo è molto gentile.
exEn: My boss is very kind.
note: Used for both men and women (il capo / la capo; plural i capi / le capo); 'la capa' is colloquial. Also means 'head' in some fixed phrases.

exEn: The director is in a meeting.
My father is a doctor.
note: Plural medici (soft c). A female doctor is usually 'la dottoressa' or still 'il medico'. No article after essere with professions: è medico.

ex: La mia insegnante di italiano è di Bologna.
exEn: My Italian teacher is from Bologna.
note: Same form for both genders: l'insegnante, un insegnante / un'insegnante.

exEn: The waiter brings the coffee.

ex: Mio zio è cuoco in un ristorante.
exEn: My uncle is a cook in a restaurant.
note: Plural with h: cuochi, cuoche.

exEn: The shop assistant is very kind.
I am a clerk in a bank.
The workers work in the factory.
My brother is an engineer.
note: Same form for both genders (l'ingegnere); for a woman the newer 'l'ingegnera' is also used.

exEn: The nurse works in the hospital.
I ask a police officer for information.
The secretary answers the phone.
My cousin is a lawyer.
note: Feminine: avvocata (also avvocatessa); many women still use 'avvocato'. 'Fare + article + profession' = to work as: fa l'avvocato.

exEn: Paolo is a journalist.
note: Same form for both genders: il/la giornalista. Plural: i giornalisti, le giornaliste.

exEn: The children go to school.
note: No article in 'a scuola' (to/at school).

ex: Nella mia classe ci sono venti studenti.
exEn: In my class there are twenty students.
The lesson starts at nine.
I am a student of Italian.
The teacher explains the lesson.
note: Students often say 'prof'. Used for secondary-school teachers, not only university professors.

exEn: The teacher reads a story.
note: Teacher at nursery/primary school; also a music master or expert.

exEn: I read a book in Italian.
I write the sentence in the notebook.
Do you have a pen?
note: Also 'feather'; 'penne' is also a pasta shape.

exEn: I draw with the pencil.
The backpack is heavy.
note: Takes the article lo / uno: lo zaino, uno zaino.

exEn: The teacher writes on the board.
note: Collocation: scrivere alla lavagna.

exEn: I do my homework after dinner.
note: 'I compiti' (plural) = homework; 'compito in classe' = written test.

ex: Domani ho un esame di storia.
exEn: Tomorrow I have a history exam.
note: Collocations: dare / fare un esame, superare un esame.

exEn: I study at the University of Bologna.
note: Invariable plural (words with a final accent do not change).

exEn: I am taking an Italian course.
note: Collocation: seguire / fare un corso.

exEn: I don't understand this word.
I speak two languages.
note: Also the body part (tongue). 'Lingua straniera' = foreign language.

exEn: Let's do the exercise on page ten.
I answer the phone.
note: 'Al telefono' = on the phone; 'numero di telefono' = phone number.

ex: Qual è il tuo numero di cellulare?
exEn: What is your mobile number?
note: Also 'telefonino' (colloquial) and 'smartphone'.

ex: Lavoro al computer tutto il giorno.
exEn: I work on the computer all day.
note: Invariable (foreign word); 'al computer' = on/at the computer.

exEn: I'll send you an email tomorrow.
note: Feminine and invariable; also written 'email' or just 'mail' (la mail).

exEn: I look for the address on the internet.
note: Feminine in dictionaries (like 'la rete'), but almost always used without an article: su internet, in internet. Also written Internet.

exEn: I'll write you a message.
note: Collocations: mandare / scrivere un messaggio.

exEn: In the evening I watch television.
note: Often shortened to 'la tv' (pronounced tivù); 'guardare la tv' = to watch TV.

ex: Mio padre legge il giornale la mattina.
exEn: My father reads the newspaper in the morning.
note: Not 'journal' (rivista, diario).

ex: Questa è una foto della mia famiglia.
exEn: This is a photo of my family.
note: Short for 'fotografia'; feminine and invariable: la foto, le foto. 'Fare una foto' = to take a photo.

exEn: Italy is a beautiful country.
note: Two meanings: a nation (often written Paese) and a village or small town (vivo in un piccolo paese).

ex: Roma è famosa in tutto il mondo.
exEn: Rome is famous all over the world.
note: 'In tutto il mondo' = all over the world.

exEn: There are many people in the square.
note: Singular collective noun: it takes a singular verb (la gente parla). 'Persone' is used for counting: tre persone.

exEn: I study Italian history.
note: Same word for 'history' and 'story'.

exEn: I'm calling the police!
note: Singular noun: la polizia è (not 'sono'). Emergency number in Italy: 112.

exEn: I work in an Italian company.

ex: La ditta di mio padre è piccola.
exEn: My father's firm is small.
note: Usually a small or family business; 'azienda' is more general.

exEn: I buy fruit at the market.
The customer pays at the till.
note: Same form for both genders: il cliente / la cliente.

exEn: My grandfather works in a factory.
note: False friend: not 'fabric' (tessuto, stoffa). Plural with h: fabbriche.

exEn: I have many things to do.
note: Also used alone as a question word: Cosa fai? = What are you doing?

exEn: No problem!
note: Masculine despite the -a ending (Greek origin): il problema, i problemi.

exEn: I have an idea!
note: 'Non ho idea' = I have no idea.

exEn: My name is Luca.
note: Surname is 'cognome'. In grammar 'nome' also means noun.

ex: La vita in città è cara.
exEn: Life in the city is expensive.
note: Do not confuse the plural 'vite' with the singular noun 'vite' (vine; screw), whose plural is 'viti'.

exEn: I do it this way.
note: 'In questo modo' = in this way; 'in ogni modo' = anyway.

exEn: Can you give me an example?
note: Collocation: fare un esempio (not 'dare'). 'Per esempio' / 'ad esempio' = for example.

exEn: I need your help.
note: 'Aiuto!' = Help! (cry for help). 'Chiedere aiuto' = to ask for help.

exEn: I need a coffee.
note: Key structure: avere bisogno di + noun/infinitive = to need.

en: good luck (literally: into the mouth of the wolf)
ex: Hai l'esame domani? In bocca al lupo!
exEn: You have the exam tomorrow? Good luck!
note: The traditional reply is 'Crepi!' (or 'Crepi il lupo!'), not 'grazie'.

exEn: A coffee, please.
note: Also 'per piacere' and (more formal) 'per cortesia'.

ex: Ci vediamo alle otto? Va bene.
exEn: See you at eight? Okay.
note: Also as a question: Va bene? = Is that okay? Colloquially shortened to 'vabbè'.

exEn: Shall we go to the cinema? Okay!
note: 'Essere d'accordo con qualcuno' = to agree with someone.

ex: Grazie per l'aiuto! Non c'è di che.
exEn: Thanks for the help! Don't mention it.
note: Reply to 'grazie', like 'prego' and 'figurati' (informal).

exEn: Thanks a lot! You're welcome.
note: Three uses: reply to grazie; inviting someone (Prego, entri! / Prego, si accomodi); asking someone to repeat (Prego?).

exEn: Sorry, do you have a moment?
note: Informal (tu). Use 'scusi' with people you address formally.

exEn: Excuse me, where is the station?
note: Formal (Lei); used to get attention from strangers, waiters, etc.

en: here is; here are; there you go; there
exEn: Here's your coffee.
note: Combines with pronouns: eccomi (here I am), eccolo (here he/it is). 'Ecco!' alone = that's it / you see!

ex: Buona fortuna per il nuovo lavoro!
exEn: Good luck with the new job!
note: More neutral than 'in bocca al lupo'; the reply is simply 'grazie'.

exEn: I'm sorry, I can't come.
note: Expresses regret; to apologise for a small thing use 'scusa/scusi'.

exEn: May I come in? Of course!
note: Also 'certo che sì' (of course yes). As an adjective certo/certa = certain, sure.

ex: Mi piace la frutta, per esempio le mele.
exEn: I like fruit, for example apples.
note: Also 'ad esempio'; abbreviated 'per es.' or 'ad es.' in writing.

en: oh my goodness; wow; good grief
exEn: Oh my, it's so hot!
note: Very common exclamation of surprise, worry or admiration.

exEn: Where is Marco? I don't know.
note: The 'lo' refers to the thing not known. Colloquial alternative: 'boh'.
